reason: The text contains multiple passages where Yahweh explicitly expresses complaints and displeasure about the people's behavior. Key instances include: (1) God's complaint through Ahijah the prophet about the people forsaking Him and worshiping false gods (יַעַן אֲשֶׁר עֲזָבוּנִי וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְעַשְׁתֹּרֶת...), stating they have not kept His commandments and statutes as David did; (2) God's rebuke of Jeroboam for his evil deeds exceeding all before him and creating golden calves to provoke God to anger (וַתָּרַע לַעֲשׂוֹת...וַתַּעֲשֶׂה־ לְּךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים); (3) Direct accusation that the man of God violated Yahweh's command (כִּי מָרִיתָ פִּי יְהוָה). These expressions of divine dissatisfaction with the people's idolatry, unfaithfulness, and violation of commandments constitute clear complaints.
